slides.title: Three iron cages that held corpses still hang on a church.
A baker who said he was Enoch
slides.body: In February 1534 Anabaptists took over Münster. Their prophet, Jan Matthys, a baker who claimed to be Enoch, said judgment would fall at Easter.

slides.title: Easter came
slides.body: On Easter Sunday he rode out against the besieging army with a small band and was killed. His head was displayed on a pole. The city fought on.

slides.title: A tailor crowned king
slides.body: Jan of Leiden, about 25, took over. He largely abolished private property, brought in polygamy and was proclaimed king, with about 16 wives.

slides.title: Starved, then betrayed
slides.body: Famine set in. In June 1535 defectors let the besiegers in. In January 1536 Jan and two other leaders were publicly tortured and killed.

slides.title: The cages are still there
slides.body: Their bodies hung in three iron cages on St Lambert's Church tower. The remains were later removed; the cages were rehung in 1898 and are still there.

caption: A baker who said he was Enoch, a tailor crowned king, and three cages that still hang in Münster. In 1987 an artist put a dim light in each one. Creepy or fitting?
xPost: Three iron cages still hang on St Lambert's Church in Münster. In 1536 they held the bodies of the leaders of an Anabaptist kingdom that had crowned a tailor of about 25 as king, with about 16 wives.
redditTitle: TIL that the three iron cages used to display the bodies of the Anabaptist 'king' Jan of Leiden and two other leaders in 1536 still hang on the tower of St Lambert's Church in Münster
